newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes tick up, but talk is subdued.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes tick up, but talk is subdued.

text.p: Deltas on some California crudes showed signs of firmness Tuesday amid refiner demand in a mostly quiet market that saw underlying NYMEX crude prices continue to retreat, traders said.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) meanwhile said crude stocks fell last week in the region by 2.5 million barrels to 67.2 million, which could inject a measure of upside potential into trade in the coming sessions.
The timing of the restart of the UN-Iraq oil-for-food deal also loomed in the minds of some players who said some of those barrels made the trip during the first round of that deal early this year.

In any case, the action was confined to home-drilled blends, while action on Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude was frozen on either side of the most recent deal closed at $2.16 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Kern River blend ticked up on talk of a deal getting done late last week at 10 cents over posted prices, or at around $13.26 a barrel. That was about 5 cents more than the most recent offers.
Also, Line 63 barrels were heard done 15 cents firmer at 90 cents over posted Buena Vista crude, or at $15.76 a barrel.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1633
